# anatomy_Q83

## Question

Patent ductus arteriosus is due to a defect in which aortic arch?

## Options

- A) 4th right
- B) 4th left
- C) 6th right
- D) 6th left ✅

## Your Answer

A) 4th right

## Correct Answer

D) 6th left

## Key Fact (generated by LLM)

Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is due to the failure of the ductus arteriosus to close after birth, and this duct is derived from the 6th left aortic arch. Normally, the ductus arteriosus closes shortly after birth, but in PDA, it remains open, allowing blood to flow from the aorta to the pulmonary artery. This defect is specifically related to the 6th left aortic arch, which is responsible for the formation of the pulmonary arteries and the ductus arteriosus.

## Why You Got It Wrong (generated by LLM)

The student incorrectly chose the 4th right aortic arch, which is not related to the development of the ductus arteriosus. This mistake suggests a lack of understanding of the embryological development of the aortic arches.
